description: I'm Marwan Sarhan, 15, from Egypt. I'm into STEM and coding. I took courses in Python, Arduino, Electronics, and Mechanics. I joined NASA Space Apps, AIO 2026, and a DivPost hackathon. I'm at New York Junior Academy. For me, skills aren't everything. I want a teammate who loves to work and engages with me, even if their skills aren't strong yet. A team should work together to reach the best result.
summary:
We built PYRO. It is a web dashboard that helps engineers choose safe materials for spacecraft. Fire in space is very different from Earth because of microgravity. NASA has a lot of research on this, but the data is big and hard to read. Engineers do not have time to read hundreds of pages.

PYRO solves this by turning complex NASA data into a simple screen. Engineers can choose a material and see its fire risk score instantly. They can also change the environment to Earth, the Moon, or Mars. The dashboard shows a live flame chamber that draws how the fire changes shape in space. It also has easy charts to compare materials and a section with safety advice.

Our project is important because it saves time and makes space travel safer for astronauts. We used real data from NASA experiments like Saffire and BASS to build it. We also used HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and the Chart.js library to build the website. All the information in PYRO is backed by real NASA sources.
details:
PYRO is a web dashboard that helps engineers choose safe materials for spacecraft. Fire in space is very different from Earth because there is no gravity. NASA has done a lot of research about this but the data is very large and hard to read. Engineers do not have time to read hundreds of pages. Our project solves this problem. We take the complex data and turn it into a simple and fast screen.

Here is how it works. The engineer opens the dashboard and uses a control panel. They can pick a material from a list like plastic or fabric. They can also pick an environment like Earth the Moon or Mars. The website then calculates a fire risk score from 0 to 100 and shows it on a big card. The app also has a live flame chamber. This is a drawing of a fire. When the engineer changes the gravity the flame changes shape. On Earth it looks like a teardrop. In space it becomes a blue sphere. This helps the engineer see the difference.

There are also two other tools. The first is a risk ranking chart. It sorts all the materials from the most dangerous to the safest. The second is a comparison chart. The engineer can pick two materials and see their properties side by side on a radar chart. The app also gives automatic safety advice. If the material is dangerous the app shows a red warning and suggests a safer material. Every number in the app has a source from NASA written under it.

The main benefit of PYRO is saving time. It helps engineers make fast and safe decisions. This is important because a wrong material choice can start a fire in a spacecraft and there is no fire department in space. We built this app using HTML and CSS for the design. We used JavaScript to make it interactive and to draw the flame animation. We used a free library called Chart dot js for the charts. For the data side we used Python and FastAPI to clean the data. We also used the NASA PSI database to get the real numbers. We did not use any special hardware just our computers.

Our project is creative because it turns hard science into a simple visual tool. We made the design look like a space command center. It has a dark blue background with stars planets and glowing orange and blue colors. We wanted the user to feel like they are in a real mission control room.

In the future we plan to add a smart assistant to the dashboard. This assistant will use Artificial Intelligence. It will not be a normal chat. It will be connected to the dashboard and will read the exact numbers that the engineer selects. For example if the engineer picks a dangerous material the assistant will talk to them and say this material is not safe here is a better option. It will give direct advice based on the NASA data. We also want to add live data from the space station and make the app work on mobile phones. Our goal is to make PYRO the best tool for space fire safety.
